points.description: States that the condition must hold for ALL possible labelings of the data points in A, i.e. all 2^N binary (positive/negative) labelings for N data points.
points.partial_credit: Says 'all labelings' or 'every labeling' but does not give 2^N or binary/positive-negative labels (or vice versa); 0.4

points.description: States that for each such labeling there is a hypothesis h (in H) that separates/splits the positive data from the negative data.
States that the separation is with no error (zero misclassification, perfectly correct on every point of A).

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three elements stated explicitly: all 2^N binary labelings, h splits positives from negatives, and with no error. Vague wording such as 'h classifies the data well' or 'h works on the dataset' earns nothing for that point. A wrong statement (e.g. only some labelings, or allowing errors) cancels the relevant point; part marks only where P1 is clearly more than half stated.
